## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kusalattika* ("Triad on the Wholesome") is the primary triad division of the *Tikapaṭṭhāna*, forming the second section of the *Paṭṭhāna* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It serves as the foundational model for the text's exhaustive inquiry into conditional relations (*paccaya*), examining how phenomena classified as wholesome (*kusala*), unwholesome (*akusala*), or indeterminate/neutral (*abyākata*) condition one another [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Its exposition is methodically organized into structural chapters such as the "dependent chapter" (*paṭicca-vāra*), systematically tracing relations under the twenty-four conditions—including root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*) and object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*)—in both positive and negative analytical modes [Nyanatiloka 2007]. In commentarial and sectarian debates, such as discussions concerning the Abhayagiri tradition's view that ascetic practices (*dhutaṅga*) are mere designations (*paññatti*), the *Kusalattika* commentary (*kusalattikavaṇṇanā*) serves as an authoritative benchmark for whether phenomena fall within or outside ultimate classifications [Chandawimala, Impact of the Abhayagiri Practices].
SuttaCentral records two translations of the *Kusalattika* across two languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies vast Pali-internal text reuse (141,154 matching passages across 318 Pali texts), demonstrating that its extensive syntactic and conditional formulas are shared across virtually the entire *Paṭṭhāna*, with its highest degrees of overlap found in adjacent triad and dyad chapters such as the *Vedanāttika* (Patthana 1.3), *Piṭṭhiduka* (Patthana 2.13), *Mahantaraduka* (Patthana 2.10), *Cūḷantaraduka* (Patthana 2.2), and *Vitakkattika* (Patthana 1.7) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text across languages with various Northern and Sanskrit Abhidharma works—including the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā*, *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya*, *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, *Dharmaskandha*, *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya*, and *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*—reflecting shared technical matrices of Abhidharma conditional and phenomenal analysis across traditions [DharmaNexus].
